title: Testing touch input headlessly in Godot
problem: Touch controls are hard to verify without a device, and naive headless tests pass vacuously.
approach: Run a SceneTree script with --headless. Set root.size explicitly (headless defaults to a 100x100 window, so layouts sized from the viewport put controls off-screen). Build InputEventScreenTouch/InputEventScreenDrag with index, position and relative, and deliver them with root.push_input(event) so they traverse _input, GUI and _unhandled_input like device input. Assert ownership and action state after each event, and assert a precondition first so later 'released' checks cannot pass vacuously.
integration: Run with tools/knowledge_godot_check.py or godot --headless --path <proj> --script res://test.gd
expected_behavior: Failures name the broken contract; the test exits non-zero.
limitations: Does not exercise OS mouse emulation from touch (Input.parse_input_event path) or real device latency

failure_modes.symptom: Most touch assertions fail or pass for no reason
failure_modes.fix: root.size = Vector2i(1280, 720) before laying out controls
